tweets.text:
Christina on why Vanta pays its top people 10x what it did five years ago

"Should I adjust the pitch and be like 'Inevitably the baseline here is Vanta's 50 billion. 

The real question you should be considering is if you join, can you take us on a journey to 250 billion?’

Should I start saying that? Probably not. But the answer is not definitely not. 

Because that is the pitch that people who work at Vanta are getting from other companies. The market now is saying that so much, you do seem unambitious.

Total comp, it's probably like a factor of 10. I think it actually should be higher. My general comp philosophy is you never pay the top people enough.

Patrick: What those top people are doing that's so valuable typically.

High agency, get shit done. That sounds so milquetoast and that's worth millions of dollars, but yes, actually it is. 

A high-context person who understands the company and the customers and the domain, making generally reasonable decisions and sometimes bad ones, and then iterating on their bad ones and just moving is so valuable."

In 2015, Boualem Sansal won the Grand Prix du roman de l’Académie française for 2084, published the same year as Michel Houellebecq’s Submission.
Sansal’s novel offered, in fact, a far darker and more pessimistic vision of the future. He imagined a religious totalitarian regime that maintains its grip on society through the manipulation of language, censorship, and, perhaps most importantly, les "non-dits," everything people are taught never to say, question, or even think about. Sansal was particularly interested in how a regime could erase historical memory so thoroughly that submission eventually feels natural. An Algerian writer of Kabyle Berber heritage and a fierce critic of the FLN regime, he was imprisoned by the Algerian authorities in 2024 and spent nearly a year behind bars while battling cancer before his release in 2025. I had the great honor of meeting his lawyer.

#Uranium #Silver #Copper #Gold
⚡ DAILY METALS PULSE | 20 October 2026
EVENING UPDATE
A potential 6 GW nuclear project. Weather-hit copper production. Silver climbing while gold slips.

☢️ URANIUM — INDIANA THINKS BIGGER
AtkinsRéalis, Hoosier Energy and Indiana have signed an agreement to explore up to EIGHT Candu reactors, totalling approximately 6 GW.

This is an early evaluation, with financing, sites and approvals still ahead. But the scale deserves attention.

Candu reactors use natural uranium fuel, adding an interesting dimension to the nuclear expansion story.

Meanwhile, Deep Yellow says equity-market conditions do not support a final investment decision on Tumas this quarter.

My takeaway: reactor ambitions keep expanding, while financing new uranium supply remains challenging.

🥈 SILVER — OUTPERFORMING GOLD

Spot silver rose 1.4% to around $57.86/oz in the latest Reuters update.

A positive divergence from gold today. I’m watching whether silver can sustain that relative strength over the coming sessions.

🔶 COPPER — SNOW HITS SUPPLY

Anglo American reported Q3 copper production of 174,900 tonnes, DOWN 5% year-on-year.

Record snowfall in Chile, related maintenance and lower-grade ore at Collahuasi weighed on output.

Full-year guidance remains unchanged at 700,000–760,000 tonnes, with improved grades expected to support Q4.

My takeaway: maintaining annual targets still requires mines to recover lost ground. High copper prices cannot prevent operational disruption.

🥇 GOLD — RATE EXPECTATIONS STILL WEIGH

Gold slipped 0.3% to around $4,126/oz. December futures settled 0.4% lower.

Markets still favour an October Fed hold, but price a roughly 92% probability of a December hike. Next week’s Fed decision and PCE inflation data remain key tests.

👀 MY WATCH

Can uranium developers secure construction funding? Can copper producers deliver their expected Q4 recovery? Can silver extend today’s outperformance?

Those are concrete tests for the metals story heading into year-end.

Follow @Swedish_Uranium for the daily pulse.

$WGS is a large position in my portfolio, and I’m adding exposure through an interesting options structure expiring November 20, with earnings in between.

I’m buying one $50 call, selling one $60 put, and selling three $80 calls, for a net credit of $1. Basically, I’m getting paid $1 per share to enter this trade.

With the stock currently at $68, if it stays at this price until expiration, I make $19 per share. My maximum profit is $31 per share if $WGS reaches $80 at expiration. I start losing money above roughly $95.50, but I would be very happy to see the stock there since I already own a large position.

I’ve made very good money on similar structures earlier this year. My real risk is a collapse in the stock, with a downside breakeven of $54, since I actually get paid to enter the trade.

Figma CEO speaks out on Claude Design: “It's easy to mistake model progress for product progress.”

Friedberg:

“How worried were you when they came out with Claude Design, relative to what you guys were offering? Because the market looked at it and said, ‘Oh my God, Figma's dead. Claude is going to crush Figma.’

Dylan Field:

“The nature of online discourse right now is, ‘We're so back, it's so over.’ And it's just a cycle, right?

I think it's easy to mistake model progress for product progress.

The reality is a tool like Figma has taken a very long time to build and a very long time to make sure that we get the workflows right for our users, and we still have work to do.

They've made Claude Design into a product that is broad. So it's trying to do a lot of things. Like, you'll see posters and stuff as well, like graphic design scenarios, I believe, when you go to their homepage.

And maybe they'll do well in some areas and not other areas. I'm not bullish or bearish on the product. I think it's just hard to make good design tools for professionals.”

The greatest tragedy of mankind is holding an opinion in your head that is wrong. It stands in the way of so many people making decisions well and operating well with each other.

It is such a tragedy because it is so easily fixed. All you have to do is put it out there and stress test it. Acknowledge the possibility of being wrong, and ask how to properly stress test that opinion. By stress testing it, you raise your probabilities of being right.

The education system, and so many things in society, reward always being right. But holding onto that mindset stands in the way of taking in all the information out there that can really help you.
#RayDalio #DecisionMaking #Principles
